## Triage: first grade, `priority:p2` · `domain:services` · `area:devpath` · `pm:queue`. Direction: a per-case timeout sized to the measured work, plus the package's own enumeration. This amends my promise of a family card

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-09T04:52Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

Triage: lands in `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-password-webcontainer.test.ts` ⇒ `domain:services`. Rationale: plugin-sharing belongs to that lane.

- **Why p2:** it intermittently reddens the required `Test Core` context: a push run on `main` and a PR run of the same commit, against a green merge group and a later green push. No assertion failed, and the hourly full run is green.
- **Why a timeout is right here, unlike #22346:**
  - That case was slow because of an accidental quadratic lookup in the test itself, so the fix removed the waste.
  - This case is deliberately CPU-bound: eight scrypt derivations at production parameters, proving that the two implementations agree.
  - Cutting the parameters would weaken what it pins. So a per-case timeout sized to its measured work, with a stated margin, is the fix, as with #21920.
  - ⛔ No skip and no quarantine. Leave the parameters alone.
- **Enumeration pin (this card closes the family inside its package):** list every case in `plugin-sharing` that runs scrypt-class derivations under the default budget, with its measured CI time. Size each one in the same PR.
- **This amends my grade `6068065094` on #22346 and my R257 record.** Both said a third timeout red would get a family card enumerating the heaviest cases. This is that third red (after #22292 and #22346).
  - A cross-package, CI-only enumeration card cannot queue under the product-only queue rule (`triage-duties.md`, batch #202 B).
  - So each case is fixed on its own card, and inside its own package, as here.
  - The cross-package duration guard that is already queued on the maintainer's direction is #16468 (the per-package suite ratchet). It works at suite level, not case level, and this card does not widen it.

Claim: PM loop round 1
Session: `session_01WYYhVJ78u7PhwFViWo1EmQ`
Account: `os-elon-musk` (the seat's linked user as `get_me` answers it; the card's assignee)

Worktree: `objectstack-issue-22418`

Seat: `domain:services#2` (seat post #21118)
File surface, per the card body and triage `6074523299`, read on `origin/main` `ca135dcc`:
- `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-password-webcontainer.test.ts`: an explicit per-case timeout on the NFKC case (about `:72`), sized to its measured work with a stated margin, and the same sizing for any sibling case in the file that the enumeration puts near the default budget.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-password.test.ts`: the other file in the package that runs scrypt-class derivations, in scope for the enumeration pin; a timeout only where its measured time calls for one.
- ⛔ No skip, no quarantine, no change to the scrypt parameters (N, r, p) or to any production file; no vitest config change; no changeset (test-only; the seat applies `skip-changeset` after checking). (Stop on breach and explain in the report.)
Container & model: `S`, `mode:subagent`, `model: default` — `dispatch-gates --tier` gives no path-derived mandate; the sizing needs measured timings and a stated margin, so the default tier.
Clause-②: no
- Test files only: no published surface, no accepted input.
Responsibility: `this repo's own test: a deliberately CPU-bound scrypt case (eight derivations at N=16384, r=16) runs under vitest's 5000 ms default, and reddens the required Test Core context at 5030–5039 ms` | `a per-case timeout sized to the measured work, as #21920 did for the same shape` | `every PR and main push whose Test Core shard carries plugin-sharing (measured on main e75dceddd7 and PR #22215)`
Thread-read: 6074523299
Serial constraints cleared: read 2026-10-09T05:10Z:
- Open PRs (17): none touches either test file. PR #22396 (this seat, #22258) edits `plugin-sharing`'s `sharing-plugin.ts` and adds `in-process-session-read.pin.test.ts`: disjoint files.
- In-flight claims in `domain:services` (seat 1): #22362 (`service-automation`), #15196 (`plugin-security`): disjoint.

<sub>`domain:services` seat 2 · `session_01WYYhVJ78u7PhwFViWo1EmQ` · read on GitHub 2026-10-09T05:59Z</sub>

**Checked on GitHub and in the diff, not from the report:**
- **Shape:** draft, base `main`; line 1 `Fixes #22418`, line 2 `Clause-②: no`; no other closing keyword; assignee `os-elon-musk`; 2 test files, +33 / −3.
- **The fix, as triage ruled (`6074523299`):** three per-case timeouts passed as the `it` third argument. Each is sized by one stated rule: a case whose slowest `Test Core` reading is over half of 5000 ms gets 3x that reading, rounded up to the next second.
  - NFKC case: 17 000 ms (projected 5515 ms, because CI cut it off at 5030 / 5039).
  - Cross-verify case: 13 000 ms (4136 / 3688 ms).
  - `share-link-password.test.ts`'s no-log case: 12 000 ms (3805 / 3417 ms).
  - The rule and the reason for each budget are in comments at the site.
  - No skip, no quarantine, no scrypt parameter change, no production file, no vitest config change.
- **Enumeration pin (PR body table):** measured, not grepped. A temporary scrypt-wrapping setup file (never committed) found 52 scrypt-reaching cases in 4 files. Local and CI readings are kept apart. Every case left on the default reads at most 43% of it, except the two `share-link-eligibility` cases, which have no CI reading; those are stated NOT MEASURED, with same-work comparisons.
- **Reproduction:** on one core beside 5 busy loops, `ca135dcc` reds the NFKC and no-log cases with `Test timed out in 5000ms`, and `616794ce` passes all 96 cases.
- **Changeset:** none, correctly. The diff is test files only, and `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` ships `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` only, so the seat applied `skip-changeset` on its own check.

**Corrections acknowledged (the seat's dispatch assumptions, falsified by measurement):**
- Assumption 1 named two files; four reach scrypt. The other two have no case near the budget, so the edit stays in the two claimed files.
- Assumption 3 (and the triage comment) cited #21920 as a per-case-timeout precedent. It landed without one (PR #21925 moved a module load into collection). The spelling follows the repo's own `it(…, budget)` convention instead.

**Out-of-scope findings:** two `carrier: none` notes go to Acceptance notes, not filed: a stale header bullet in `share-link-password.test.ts`, and the #21920 citation above.

**Owed before landing:** every check green on `616794ce`.

**At landing (`Fixes`):** the seat confirms the card closed and clears `pm:dispatched` and the assignee.
